subsystems.name: Tissue preparation and imaging
subsystems.role: captures the brain's wiring at synapse resolution without destroying it.
parts: serial block-face or focused-ion-beam electron microscope

subsystems.name: Image reconstruction pipeline
subsystems.role: turns petabytes of micrographs into a usable wiring diagram.

subsystems.name: Connectome data model
subsystems.role: stores every neuron, process and synapse with its strength and type.

subsystems.name: Biophysical simulation
subsystems.role: reproduces the electrical behaviour of the network in software.

subsystems.name: Compute substrate
subsystems.role: runs the simulation fast enough to behave in real time.

subsystems.name: Interface and embodiment
subsystems.role: lets the simulated mind sense, act and communicate.

buildSteps.title: Preserve the tissue
buildSteps.detail: The brain is fixed and stained so membranes and synapses stay visible under an electron beam — currently a destructive step, so the original is not preserved.

buildSteps.title: Image every cubic millimetre
buildSteps.detail: A serial block-face microscope cuts away nanometre-thin layers and photographs each freshly exposed surface, producing millions of images per cubic millimetre.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct the cells
buildSteps.detail: Software aligns the images and traces every neuron's branching processes through the volume, correcting errors by hand where the algorithms fail.

buildSteps.title: Identify the synapses
buildSteps.detail: Each connection is located, classified (excitatory or inhibitory, and by neurotransmitter) and given an estimated strength.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the model
buildSteps.detail: The connectome is converted into a mathematical network of neurons and connections, with dynamics fitted from electrophysiology.

buildSteps.title: Simulate it
buildSteps.detail: The network is run on large accelerator clusters; a whole human brain at this detail implies exascale-and-beyond computing.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and validate
buildSteps.detail: Simulated activity is compared against real recordings — first single-neuron behaviour, then whole circuits, then outward behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop with a body
buildSteps.detail: The simulation is connected to sensors and actuators so it can act in the world, which is also how you would test whether it is functioning.

buildSteps.title: Confront identity and consent
buildSteps.detail: Any claim of a hosted mind raises unresolved questions of consent, rights and whether a copy counts as the same person — no technical method settles this.

prerequisites.why: the full connectome of a fruit fly was published in 2024 and a cubic-millimetre volume of mouse cortex has been mapped, but no mammal's whole brain has been.
every current method fixes and slices the brain, so the person is not preserved by the scan itself.
the largest supercomputers exist, but whole-brain simulation at this fidelity would demand far more.

prerequisites.tech: A theory linking neural activity to cognition
prerequisites.why: without it, a perfect wiring diagram could be rebuilt and still produce nothing recognisable as a mind.
thousands of channels have been demonstrated in humans; millions would be needed to match a brain's throughput.

pathway.milestone: complete connectomes of small animals and small cortical volumes of mammals
pathway.unlocks: automated reconstruction tools and the first testable network models.

pathway.milestone: a full mouse brain connectome plus simulation reproducing learned behaviours
pathway.unlocks: evidence that structure alone carries enough information to reproduce function.

pathway.milestone: non-destructive, high-resolution scanning of a living brain
pathway.unlocks: the possibility of mapping a specific person rather than an average one.

pathway.milestone: real-time simulation of a human-scale network on a non-biological substrate
pathway.unlocks: the only route by which 'mind uploading' could be attempted at all — and even then, whether the result is the same person is untestable.
